To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the geospatial distance between production and consumption is increasing, which leads to an increased displacement of environmental and health impacts through international trade, and that this is particularly true for the trade of manufactured goods.
international trade leads to the displacement of environmental and socio economic impacts from affluent to developing countries.
the environmental and social foot prints of international trade are substantial and increasing, and that they are often not reflected by conventional sustainability indicators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the geospatial distribution of consumption and production is linked with the distribution of environmental and social costs, and how these linkages are changing over time.
the environmental and social impacts of international trade and their geospatial separation from consumption.
how to measure the environmental and social foot prints of global production and trade and the implications of this for the implementation of the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the geospatial displacement of impacts through trade is an issue that needs to be addressed by policy.
the environmental and social impacts of international trade have increased, and that the direction of impact displacement has been from developed countries to developing countries.
international trade has a strong impact on the environmental and social footprint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the environmental and social foot-prints of international trade should be included in national sustainability assessments to avoid loopholes and to achieve a comprehensive implementation of the UN Sustainable Development Goal.
we have shown the need for the inclusion of footprint information in the implementation of the SDGs and the importance of the inclusion of trade related information.
international trade has increased the geospatial distance between production and consumption, with a consequent displacement of environmental and health impacts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
international trade can be a powerful driver of environmental and social progress or a major barrier to it.
international trade has led to a displacement of environmental and health impacts from affluent countries towards developing ones.
the environmental and social impacts of international trade are substantial and increasing, and that the trend is likely to continue.
